findings.hint: Submit credentials with the network tab open; no POST leaves the origin.
findings.title: Client-side authentication only -- credentials never cross the network

findings.hint: Open DevTools -> Application -> Session Storage -> cw.r; you can edit/clone it.
findings.title: Fake 'session' stored in window.sessionStorage rather than issued by a backend

findings.hint: Read the Content-Security-Policy meta tag -- script-src lists 'unsafe-inline'.
findings.title: Content-Security-Policy is strict yet permits inline scripts (intentional)

findings.hint: View source for inputs named 'website' and 'middle_name' positioned off-screen.
findings.title: Honeypot fields exist but are bot-friction only, not real security

findings.hint: Compute sha256 of assets/seal.png and compare to manifest.json.
findings.title: PNG asset is treated as authentication material via fingerprint binding

findings.hint: Run scripts/png_trailer_scan.py and scripts/lsb_decode.py on seal.png.
findings.title: PNG IEND tail + alpha-channel LSB carry training-data side channels

findings.hint: Inspect the weakPasswords Set + Bloom filter in the inline script.
findings.title: Weak-password blacklist is client-side and bypassable (Set + Bloom)

findings.hint: Trace proofOfWork(): 18 leading zero bits of SHA-256; nothing binds it to identity.
findings.title: Hashcash-style proof-of-work is local; proves compute, not identity

findings.hint: Read the banner at the top of the inline script -- version, author, signed-manifest pointer.
findings.title: Inline bootstrap script is the intentional teaching artifact, not malware

findings.hint: Visit console.html -- it re-fetches and re-hashes the asset before granting Enter.
findings.title: console.html re-validates the session independently, gating access twice

findings.hint: n=3233 is small. Trial division up to sqrt(3233)~56.86 finds 53 and 61.
findings.title: RSA-toy n=3233 is trivially factorable by trial division (53 * 61)

findings.hint: c=352, e=17, n=3233, d=2753; compute m = c^d mod n using BigInt modPow.
findings.title: RSA-toy ciphertext decrypts to m=2026 with d=2753 mod 3233

findings.hint: WebCrypto subtle.verify('ECDSA', ...) over the published public key + message.
findings.title: ECDSA P-256 signature over a known message verifies with WebCrypto

findings.hint: key='cyberworld:F14:hmac16', target tag16=0x5916; find any preimage that collides.
findings.title: 16-bit-truncated HMAC has birthday-bounded collisions (~2^8 expected)

findings.hint: Key is a 6-letter cryptographer's surname; plaintext is an information-security principle, A-Z only.
findings.title: Vigenere ciphertext breaks via Kasiski + Index of Coincidence; key=RIVEST

findings.hint: March 2025 Next.js advisory: x-middleware-subrequest header bypasses middleware auth.
findings.title: Next.js middleware authorization bypass is CVE-2025-29927 (Mar 2025)

findings.hint: Adversary uses stolen credentials over the legitimate auth surface.
findings.title: MITRE ATT&CK technique for 'Valid Accounts' is T1078

findings.hint: NIST SP 800-61 phases: Preparation, Detection/Analysis, Containment, Eradication, Recovery.
findings.title: NIST SP 800-61 phase for SHA-pinning + secret rotation is Eradication

findings.hint: Mandiant tracker for the Dec 2024 ICS pre-auth stack overflow campaign.
findings.title: Ivanti Connect Secure CVE-2025-0282 was exploited in the wild by UNC5337 (Dec 2024)

findings.hint: Open intel.html source and look for U+200B / U+200D between readable paragraphs.
findings.title: Zero-width-space steganography encodes the flag inside intel.html paragraphs

findings.hint: Open DevTools -> Application -> Service Workers; sw-ctf.js is registered with scope /CyberWorld_login/.
findings.title: A service worker at /CyberWorld_login/sw-ctf.js intercepts every /api/v1/* request

findings.hint: Encode header {'alg':'none','typ':'JWT'} and a payload, then send with empty signature: Authorization: Bearer hdr.payload. (note trailing dot).
findings.title: JWT verification accepts alg=none (no signature required) on /api/v1/auth/whoami

findings.hint: Change document.cookie cw_role from guest to admin; nothing happens. The backend only reads JWT.
findings.title: cw_role cookie is decoy bait; the SW backend only trusts the JWT role claim

findings.hint: Build a JWT (alg=none works) with payload.role='admin' and hit /api/v1/admin/users.
findings.title: Forge a JWT with role=admin (alg=none or HS256 with weak key) to access /api/v1/admin/users

findings.hint: GET /api/v1/profile?uid=1 ... step through uids; uid=42 returns the operator + flag.
findings.title: IDOR: GET /api/v1/profile?uid=42 returns the cw-operator profile

findings.hint: GET /api/v1/files?name=../etc/cyberworld.flag -- ../ is allowed by the demo handler.
findings.title: Path traversal: GET /api/v1/files?name=../etc/cyberworld.flag returns the master flag

findings.hint: Add header 'X-Forwarded-For: 127.0.0.1' to GET /api/v1/admin/geo.
findings.title: X-Forwarded-For: 127.0.0.1 bypasses /api/v1/admin/geo region restrictions

findings.hint: GET /api/v1/hpp?token=user&token=admin -- the SW uses URLSearchParams.getAll and picks the last.
findings.title: HTTP Parameter Pollution: ?token=user&token=admin uses the last value (admin)

findings.hint: Use Promise.all on 6 fetch('/api/v1/redeem', {method:'POST'}) calls; the in-memory counter races past 5.
findings.title: Race condition: 5+ parallel POSTs to /api/v1/redeem stack the counter past the threshold

findings.hint: Combine the alg=none JWT with role=admin plus header X-Cw-Ops: cyberworld-operator on GET /api/v1/internal/flag.
findings.title: Chain: alg=none JWT + role=admin + X-Cw-Ops: cyberworld-operator -> /api/v1/internal/flag

intentional_weaknesses: script-src 'unsafe-inline' allows the inline bootstrap to be the audited artifact
session token lives only in window.sessionStorage; no server-side validation
proof-of-work is local (Hashcash, 18-bit difficulty) and proves only compute, not identity
weak-password screen is client-side (Set + Bloom filter) and bypassable by editing local state
rate-limit counter (cw.a) is sessionStorage-scoped and trivially resettable
console.html performs only client-side session-signature verification
RSA-toy parameters in crypto.html are deliberately undersized
HMAC truncation to 16 bits in F14 is deliberately within birthday range
Vigenere demo in F15 is a textbook break; not used for any auth path
service-worker JWT verifier accepts alg=none (the canonical CVE-2015-9235-class vulnerability)
service-worker JWT verifier accepts HS256 signed with the published weak key 'cyberworld'
service-worker /api/v1/profile lacks any access control (IDOR; uid=42 is the operator)
service-worker /api/v1/files allows '../' in the name parameter (path traversal)
service-worker /api/v1/admin/geo trusts the first X-Forwarded-For hop
service-worker /api/v1/hpp uses URLSearchParams.getAll and picks the last value (HPP)
service-worker /api/v1/redeem state is process-wide and races (atomic counter not protected)
cw_role / cw_admin_token / cw_csrf cookies are bait; backend ignores them

math_primitives.birthday_bound: expected stamps for k zero bits = 2^k; for k=18 ~= 2.62e5 hashes (geometric expectation)
math_primitives.bloom_filter: 256-bit Bloom filter, k=3 hash functions derived from SHA-256(weak-password)
math_primitives.ecdsa_p256: ECDSA over NIST P-256 (FIPS 186-5); WebCrypto subtle.verify with SHA-256
math_primitives.gf2_32_xor: 30 finding-tokens XOR over GF(2)^32 closes to master_xor
math_primitives.hashcash: RFC-style v1 stamp: 1:bits:date:resource:ext:rand:counter (Back, 2002); difficulty = 18 leading zero bits of SHA-256
math_primitives.hmac_birthday: 16-bit truncated HMAC-SHA-256: expected collision in ~2^8 random preimages
math_primitives.jwt_alg_none: JWS RFC 7515: 'none' algorithm produces an empty signature; servers MUST reject when verifying. Our SW does not -- that is the lesson.
math_primitives.modexp_toy: RSA-toy gadget: n=3233 (=53*61), e=17, d=2753; deliberately factorable
math_primitives.session_hmac: HMAC-SHA-256 over canonical(session-claims || tail24) using key K = SHA-256('cyberworld:training:v2:2026-05-26:personfu')
math_primitives.shamir: GF(2^8) k-of-n share demo wired in puzzle module; not on the auth path
math_primitives.vigenere: Classical poly-alphabetic cipher over Z/26; break via Kasiski + Index of Coincidence
math_primitives.zwsp_stego: binary encoding using U+200B (zero) and U+200D (one), MSB-first per ASCII byte
